This process often involves collecting data on various ecological indicators, such as species populations, habitat conditions, and water quality, to inform conservation efforts and management practices.

In the context of the entities provided, ecological monitoring can be seen in initiatives like the WRIA 1 Salmon Recovery Program, which focuses on monitoring salmon populations and their habitats in the Nooksack Basin of Whatcom County, Washington. This program involves local governments and community organizations to ensure the recovery of salmon populations through habitat restoration and protection projects.

Additionally, ecological sensing agents, such as those in the Colorado River Basin, utilize technology and data to enhance monitoring efforts, contributing to bioregional ecological stewardship and informed decision-making.
